content:
We've been using iOS 27 for about two months now. Of course, it's still a beta version, and the official public release is another 4 to 6 weeks away. That said, even though I've been running the beta on my phone for the past two months, honestly, I haven't really paid much attention to it. It just... works.

Of course, I still rush to open the Software Update screen every couple of weeks to grab the latest beta. That's the only part of the beta experience that stays consistent with the iOS 27 cycle.

Beyond that, I can't think of any of the usual beta issues. Battery drain is essentially nonexistent, the phone isn't overheating, there are no weird glitches or stutters, and it doesn't randomly crash.

iOS 27 brings all the benefits of new software, like Siri AI, AirPods EQ, new Wallet passes in Safari, beefed-up Photos AI editing, and so on—but without any of the downsides that usually come with running bleeding-edge beta software. Honestly, it's a bit surprising.

Perhaps that's because iOS 26 itself wasn't exactly stable to begin with. iOS 26.5 in particular, at least for me personally, somehow started making my phone respring constantly (the software crashes, and the screen goes black with a loading indicator).

These are all personal anecdotes, of course, but ask virtually anyone, and you'll hear some kind of story about iOS 26 not performing well.

iOS 27 is genuinely excellent

All in all, iOS 27 delivers when it comes to speed improvements, bug fixes, stability, and quality-of-life enhancements. You might not notice at first because there's a lot of indexing happening in the background for Siri AI—but Apple recently rolled out iOS 26.6, which starts the Siri AI background indexing for you, so you won't have to deal with that yourself when you upgrade to iOS 27. After that, it's smooth sailing.

I'm really looking forward to the general public getting their hands on iOS 27 when it releases next month. It's hard to believe, but Apple really does seem to have fixed all of iOS's major annoyances. Of course, it's not perfect—software never is—but this is absolutely the best my iPhone has felt in years.

iOS 27 will support every iPhone model that can run iOS 26, meaning the iPhone 11 and up will all get the update.
